subject: FinBridge — access trace samples, delivery options, and retention scope
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finbridge.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: sample exports for 'who accessed what' + retention question

Hi Emily — great call this morning, thanks for walking through the FinBridge use cases. A quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same scope: 

- You asked for a sample export showing "who accessed what/when" across the last 30 days, scoped to three service clusters (payments, reconciliation, reporting).
- Format preferences you mentioned: CSV for quick review, Parquet if we can do a compressed columnar export for the security team.
- Retention ask: your auditors want our retention policy for access logs, plus a sample demonstrating data residency and how long "who-viewed-what" traces are kept before archival.

Can you confirm: the sample should include requester, resource path, action (read/write/token-use), result (allowed/denied), and timestamp, and you prefer UTC timestamps in ISO8601. Also confirm whether the security team needs PII redaction on the sample (we can redact usernames / email addresses or pseudonymize).

I attached a proposed CSV schema (finbridge_log_schema_v1.csv) and a small Parquet sample we usually send for these requests (access_sample.parquet.zip) — those are example formats, not actual customer data. Once you confirm the exact fields and any redaction rules we will export a sanitized 30-day sample from our staging retention store.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm required fields + redaction level (by EOD 9/14).
2) We produce a sanitized sample within 48 hours and share a secure S3 presigned URL or a Drive folder (your preference).
3) If the sample looks good, we map the full retention policy and provide a signed evidence pack (schema, extract method, hashes, and residency statement).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15-min call if that helps.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

[Attachment: finbridge_log_schema_v1.csv (1 KB)]
[Attachment: access_sample.parquet.zip (2.3 MB)]

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finbridge.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: secureops@finbridge.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample exports for 'who accessed what' + retention question

Thanks Jonas — useful recap. Quick answers inline: 

- Fields: requester_id (email), requester_role, resource_id, resource_type, action, action_result, timestamp_utc, session_id, originating_ip. The security team will also want the model / endpoint id for inference calls.
- Format: we prefer Parquet for initial review (smaller and easier to run queries) but please provide a CSV variant we can open without Spark.
- Redaction: for the sample please pseudonymize requester_id (keep consistent pseudonyms so we can trace behavior across sessions). No need to include raw PII in the sample. For the production export we will require a signed statement that raw requester emails are not included in the exported file and a log of who had access to the raw logs.
- Retention: please include your standard retention windows, plus any cold-archive policies. FinBridge compliance currently needs a clear statement of who can retrieve raw logs and for how long (we require 90 days hot, 365 days cold archival visibility).

If you can deliver the sanitized Parquet + CSV sample by 9/16 EOD that would be great. Also include a short note on how you compute "who accessed what" when requests are proxied through internal service accounts.

Emily Zhao
Dir, Security Operations, FinBridge
emily.zhao@finbridge.com

----Original message attached----

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-demo: sample exports for 'who accessed what' + retention question

Jonas — looping in Marissa to run the extract. Quick internal notes: 

- We should provide both Parquet (partitioned by date) and a flattened CSV sample (max 10k rows) with pseudonymization applied. Use stable hashing on emails for pseudonyms (sha256 truncated) and include a salt file in the evidence pack (salt itself stored only in the security artifacts, not in the sample).
- For provenance, include a small MD5/SHA256 manifest per file and a short readme that documents the query used against the retention store (timestamp range, dataset id).
- Regarding "who can retrieve raw logs": we will provide an RBAC statement and an access list snapshot (who had permissions at the time of export). That can be exported as JSON but for the evidence pack we'll include a human-readable CSV.

Marissa — can you run the pipeline with the following parameters?
- date_range: 2026-08-15 to 2026-09-14
- partitions: daily
- fields: as Emily requested + endpoint_id
- pseudonymization: stable hash (sha256) on requester_id
- output: s3 presigned URL (7 day expiry) + Drive copy for FinBridge security team

We should aim to have the sample + manifest by Thursday 9/16 EOD. Let me know if any infra constraints.

Thanks,
Ben
Security Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_manifest_template.csv (2 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@finbridge.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: sample exports for 'who accessed what' + retention question

Emily — sample extract is ready and uploaded. Delivery details below. Also included a short QA note on residency and access controls.

Delivery: 
- Parquet: s3://redwood-evidence/DB-4721/finbridge_access_sample_20260914.parquet (shared via presigned link: https://s3-presigned.example/finbridge_access_sample_20260914.parquet?X-Amz-Expires=604800)
- CSV (flattened, first 10k rows): Google Drive folder (view-only): https://drive.google.com/finbridge-evidence-samples

Attachments included in the evidence pack: finbridge_log_schema_v1.csv, access_sample.parquet.zip (sanitized), extract_manifest_20260914.csv, access_rbac_snapshot_20260914.csv

QA notes (short): 
- Residency: all extracted samples were generated from the US-central regional retention store. No raw PII was exported — requester_id fields were pseudonymized with a stable hash.
- Retention statement: Redwood hot retention for access traces is 90 days by default; cold archival (read-only) retained for 365 days. We attach the retention policy excerpt in the evidence pack.
- Provenance: each file has an accompanying SHA256 checksum; the manifest lists the query parameters used to produce the extract.

If this looks good, Jonas — I'll prepare the signed evidence pack (PDF + checksums + RBAC snapshot) and a short statement on how proxied service accounts are resolved (we include a resolved_actor field that maps proxy->originating_user where available). Planning to have the signed pack by Friday 9/17.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment: extract_manifest_20260914.csv (3 KB)]
